crusadecraft.army.formation.unknown: Unknown formation: masse, ligne, colonne or carre.
crusadecraft.war.army.muster.tip: Brings the army into the world as real soldiers. You must stand near a built military camp of the realm.
crusadecraft.war.army.follow.tip: The mustered soldiers follow you, in their formation.
crusadecraft.war.army.hold.tip: The soldiers guard the spot where you stand, facing where you look.
crusadecraft.war.army.formation.tip: Changes the formation: massed, in line (two ranks), in column (in pairs), in square.
crusadecraft.war.army.dismiss.tip: The soldiers go home; the men stay counted in the army.
crusadecraft.army.pawn.beaten: Beaten: it is re-forming at home
crusadecraft.toast.host.title: Battle!
crusadecraft.toast.host.body: The host of %s faces you: %s soldier(s).
crusadecraft.toast.host_beaten.title: Host beaten
crusadecraft.warmap.tool.march.tip: Click the map: your mustered army marches there, in its formation (in stages, loaded chunks only).
crusadecraft.warmap.hint.march: Click where your army should march
crusadecraft.codex.armee.p2: From the war screen: $(l)Muster$(), $(l)Follow$(), $(l)Hold$(), the $(l)formation$() (massed, line, column, square) and $(l)Dismiss$(). On the map, in $(l)War$() mode, the $(l)March$() tool sends the army where you click.$(br2)At war, each computer realm raises a $(l)host$() that marches on the map and on Dynmap. When your army reaches it, it appears as real soldiers: beating it adds to the war score.
